form.en: old-style poem, seven characters a line

text_note.zh: 原始文本第二句作“枣花未落桐阴长”。通行本多作“枣花未落桐叶长”，这里用通行本。
text_note.en: In the corpus text, line two says the shade of the paulownia trees grows long. Most common editions say the paulownia leaves grow long instead, and that is followed here.

readings.zh: “长”这里是生长的意思，读 zhǎng。
readings.en: Here this character means "to grow", so it is read zhǎng, not cháng.

readings.zh: “朝”这里是早晨的意思，读 zhāo。
readings.en: Here this character means "morning", so it is read zhāo.

readings.zh: 这里一般读 hái，意思是“还能、又”。一说读 huán，意思是“回来”。
readings.en: This is usually read hái, meaning "still" or "again". Another view reads it huán, "to come back".

readings.zh: “饮我曹”是请我们喝酒，“饮”读 yìn。
readings.en: In "giving us drink", this character means to make someone drink, and is read yìn.

glosses.zh: 桐叶长：梧桐树的叶子长大了。
glosses.en: tóng yè zhǎng: the paulownia leaves have grown big.

glosses.zh: 朝别暮还见：早上告别了青山，到傍晚还能望见它。写一路上依依不舍。
glosses.en: zhāo bié mù hái jiàn: he leaves the green hills in the morning and can still see them at dusk. It shows how slowly, how unwillingly he goes.

glosses.zh: 嘶马：叫着的马。嘶，马叫。
glosses.en: sī mǎ: a neighing horse. Sī is a horse's cry.

glosses.zh: 旧乡：故乡，老家。
glosses.en: jiù xiāng: one's old home.

glosses.zh: 陈侯：对陈章甫的尊称，像说“陈先生”。
glosses.en: chén hóu: a polite way to address Chen Zhangfu, like "Lord Chen".

glosses.zh: 立身：做人，为人处世。
glosses.en: lì shēn: how one lives and behaves.

glosses.zh: 坦荡：心胸宽广，光明磊落。
glosses.en: tǎn dàng: open-hearted and honest.

glosses.zh: 虬须：卷曲的胡子。虬，传说中有角的小龙，这里形容弯曲。
glosses.en: qiú xū: a curly beard. Qiú is a small horned dragon, used here for something twisting.

glosses.zh: 大颡：宽大的额头。颡，额头。
glosses.en: dà sǎng: a broad forehead. Sǎng means forehead.

glosses.zh: 贮书：装着书。贮，存放。这里说他读书很多。
glosses.en: zhù shū: holding books. Zhù means to store. It says he has read a great deal.

glosses.zh: 草莽：草野，指民间，不做官的地方。
glosses.en: cǎo mǎng: the wild grass, meaning among common people, out of office.

glosses.zh: 不肯低头：不愿意向别人低声下气。
glosses.en: bù kěn dī tóu: unwilling to bow down to anyone.

glosses.zh: 东门：洛阳城的东门，一般是送别的地方。
glosses.en: dōng mén: the east gate of the city, where people saw friends off.

glosses.zh: 酤酒：买酒。
glosses.en: gū jiǔ: to buy wine.

glosses.zh: 饮我曹：请我们喝酒。我曹，我们。
glosses.en: yìn wǒ cáo: to treat us to drinks. Wǒ cáo means we, us.

glosses.zh: 鸿毛：大雁的羽毛，比喻很轻、不值一提。
glosses.en: hóng máo: a wild goose's feather, a picture of something very light, not worth caring about.

glosses.zh: 空望：无事地望着，出神地看。
glosses.en: kōng wàng: to gaze idly, lost in thought.

glosses.zh: 长河：指黄河。
glosses.en: cháng hé: the long river, meaning the Yellow River.

glosses.zh: 津口：渡口，坐船过河的地方。
glosses.en: jīn kǒu: a ferry crossing.

glosses.zh: 郑国游人：郑地来的游子。一般认为指陈章甫，一说指诗人自己。郑国，春秋时的国名，在今天的河南。
glosses.en: zhèng guó yóu rén: the traveller from Zheng. It usually means Chen Zhangfu; another view says the poet himself. Zheng was an ancient state in today's Henan.

glosses.zh: 未及家：还没能回到家。
glosses.en: wèi jí jiā: not yet able to reach home.

glosses.zh: 洛阳行子：洛阳的过客。一般认为指诗人自己，一说指陈章甫。
glosses.en: luò yáng xíng zǐ: the traveller in Luoyang. Usually the poet himself; another view says Chen Zhangfu.

glosses.zh: 闻道：听说。
glosses.en: wén dào: I hear that.

glosses.zh: 故林：老家的树林，指故乡。
glosses.en: gù lín: the woods of home, meaning one's hometown.

translation.zh: 四月里吹着南风，大麦已经黄了，
translation.en: In the fourth month the south wind blows and the barley turns gold.

translation.zh: 枣花还没落，梧桐树的叶子已经长大。
translation.en: The jujube flowers have not yet fallen, and the paulownia leaves have grown.

translation.zh: 早上告别了青山，傍晚还能望见它，
translation.en: You leave the green hills in the morning and can still see them at dusk.

translation.zh: 马儿嘶叫着出了门，你想念着故乡。
translation.en: Your horse neighs as you ride out the gate, longing for your old home.

translation.zh: 陈先生做人多么光明磊落，
translation.en: Lord Chen, how open and honest you are!

translation.zh: 卷曲的胡子，老虎一样的眉毛，还有宽宽的额头。
translation.en: A curly beard, tiger brows, and a broad forehead.
Ten thousand scrolls of books are stored in your belly.
You will not bow your head, though you live among common folk.

translation.zh: 在东门买来酒请我们喝，
translation.en: At the east gate you buy wine and treat us all.

translation.zh: 心里把万事都看得像鸿毛一样轻。
translation.en: In your heart all worldly things weigh no more than a goose feather.

translation.zh: 喝醉了躺下，连天黑了都不知道，
translation.en: Drunk, you lie down and never notice the day has ended.

translation.zh: 有时出神地望着高空里的一朵孤云。
translation.en: Sometimes you gaze idly at a lonely cloud high in the sky.

translation.zh: 黄河上的浪头连着天，黑沉沉的，
translation.en: On the Yellow River the waves reach the sky, dark and heavy.

translation.zh: 渡口的船都停下了，过不了河。
translation.en: At the ferry the boats have stopped; no one can cross.

translation.zh: 郑地来的游子还没能回到家，
translation.en: The traveller from Zheng has not reached home yet.

translation.zh: 洛阳的过客只能白白叹气。
translation.en: The traveller in Luoyang can only sigh in vain.

translation.zh: 听说你老家有很多老朋友，
translation.en: I hear you have many old friends back home.

translation.zh: 昨天刚丢了官，现在他们会怎么待你呢？
translation.en: You lost your post just yesterday; how will they treat you now?

background.zh: 陈章甫是李颀的朋友，一般说他是江陵人，曾经在嵩山隐居，很有学问。这首诗写的是他丢了官、准备回乡时，李颀为他送行。从诗里看，送别是在初夏四月，地点大概在洛阳一带，碰上黄河风浪大，船过不了河。具体是哪一年，没有确切记载。
background.en: Chen Zhangfu was Li Qi's friend. He is usually said to have come from Jiangling, to have lived as a hermit on Mount Song for a time, and to have been very learned. This poem was written when Chen had lost his official post and was about to go home, and Li Qi saw him off. From the poem we can tell it was early summer, in the fourth month, probably near Luoyang, and the Yellow River was too rough for the ferries to cross. The exact year is not recorded.

author_note.zh: 李颀，唐代诗人，生活在唐玄宗开元、天宝年间。他考中过进士，只做过县尉这样的小官，后来辞官回家隐居。他和王维、高适等人都有来往，擅长写人物，几笔就能把一个人写活。这首诗里的陈章甫，就写得很有神气。
author_note.en: Li Qi was a Tang poet who lived during the reign of Emperor Xuanzong. He passed the top civil exam but only held small posts such as county officer, and later quit to live quietly at home. He knew poets like Wang Wei and Gao Shi. He was good at portraits in words; with a few strokes he could bring a person to life, as he does with Chen Zhangfu here.

appreciation.zh: 这是一首送别诗，可一点也不哭哭啼啼。开头四句是初夏的风景：麦子黄了，枣花开着，桐叶长大，朋友骑马上路。中间八句给陈章甫画像：胡子卷，眉毛像老虎，肚子里有万卷书，不肯向人低头，喝酒请客，醉了就睡，看着孤云发呆。一个又豪爽又有点傲气的读书人站在我们眼前。最后六句回到眼前：黄河浪大，船过不去，两个人都只能叹气。结尾一问“今如何”，又关心又担心：你丢了官回家，老朋友们还会像从前一样对你吗？
appreciation.en: This is a farewell poem, but there is no weeping in it. The first four lines show early summer: gold barley, jujube flowers, big paulownia leaves, and a friend riding off. The middle eight lines paint Chen Zhangfu: a curly beard, tiger brows, ten thousand books in his belly, a man who will not bow to anyone, who buys the wine, sleeps when drunk, and stares at a lonely cloud. A bold, slightly proud scholar stands before us. The last six lines return to the moment: the Yellow River is rough, the boats cannot cross, and both men can only sigh. The closing question, how is it now, is full of care and worry: you have lost your post, so will your old friends still treat you as before?
